subtopic: Assessment For/Of/As Learning, Validity/Reliability, Rubrics, & Item Analysis

items.definition: Assessment conducted during the instructional process to monitor learner progress, diagnose learning gaps, and provide immediate descriptive feedback to adjust teaching and learning.
items.rationalization: Formative assessment is not graded; its primary objective is to inform instruction and improve student learning before summative grading.

mnemonic.title: Assessment FOR Learning
mnemonic.phrase: FOR Feeding Progress and Informing Practice

items.tosCompetency: Distinguish Assessment FOR, OF, and AS Learning

items.definition: Assessment administered at the conclusion of an instructional unit, term, or semester to certify mastery, determine grades, evaluate program efficacy, and report achievement.
items.rationalization: Summative assessment is evaluative and graded; examples include quarterly exams, final projects, standardized achievement tests, and Licensure Exams.

mnemonic.title: Assessment OF Learning
mnemonic.phrase: OF is the Official Final Score

items.tosCompetency: Distinguish Assessment FOR, OF, and AS Learning

items.definition: Assessment that engages students as active participants who monitor their own thinking, self-assess against clear criteria, set personal goals, and reflect on their learning journey.
items.rationalization: Develops metacognitive awareness and autonomous self-regulation through student self-assessment and peer reflection checklists.

mnemonic.title: Assessment AS Learning
mnemonic.phrase: AS = Autonomous Self-Monitoring

items.tosCompetency: Distinguish Assessment FOR, OF, and AS Learning

items.definition: Pre-instructional assessment designed to identify students' specific strengths, recurring weaknesses, misconceptions, and learning deficits prior to teaching.
items.rationalization: Unlike general pre-tests, diagnostic tests pinpoint specific underlying conceptual errors (e.g., misapplying decimal placement in division).

mnemonic.title: Diagnostic Assessment
mnemonic.phrase: Diagnosing Defects Before Designing Direction

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate types of assessment according to purpose

items.definition: Assessment administered at the start of an academic course or program to determine entry-level prerequisites and assign learners into appropriate tracks, levels, or classes.
items.rationalization: Examples include college entrance exams, language proficiency placement tests, or reading level readiness inventories.

mnemonic.title: Placement Assessment
mnemonic.phrase: Placing Pupils in Proper Positions

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate types of assessment according to purpose

items.definition: Assessment requiring learners to apply knowledge and skills to perform realistic, real-world, meaningful tasks (e.g., conducting an experiment, staging a debate, building a model, publishing a newsletter).
items.rationalization: Directly evaluates real competence in context, contrasting with indirect paper-and-pencil multiple-choice tests.

mnemonic.title: Authentic Assessment
mnemonic.phrase: Authentic Action in the Real World

items.tosCompetency: Design authentic and performance-based assessments

items.definition: Conventional assessment methods typically utilizing indirect paper-and-pencil standardized tests, multiple-choice items, true-or-false, and matching types.
items.rationalization: Highly efficient for testing large numbers of students on broad cognitive content, but limited in measuring practical psychomotor and real-world skills.

mnemonic.title: Traditional Assessment
mnemonic.phrase: Paper, Pencil, and Prompt Recall

items.tosCompetency: Compare traditional and authentic assessment modalities

items.definition: The extent to which an assessment tool adequately and representatively samples the full domain of content, topics, and objectives intended to be measured.
items.rationalization: Guaranteed by constructing and strictly adhering to a well-balanced Table of Specifications (TOS).

mnemonic.title: Content Validity
mnemonic.phrase: TOS Guarantees Thorough Content

items.tosCompetency: Analyze types of validity in educational measurement

items.definition: The degree to which a test measures the hypothetical psychological construct, trait, or psychological theory it claims to measure (e.g., intelligence, creativity, critical thinking).
items.rationalization: Verified through factor analysis and convergent/discriminant validity testing with related theoretical constructs.

mnemonic.title: Construct Validity
mnemonic.phrase: Capturing the Core Psychological Construct

items.tosCompetency: Analyze types of validity in educational measurement

items.definition: Criterion validity correlates test scores with an external criterion; Concurrent validity measures against a current established benchmark simultaneously; Predictive validity forecasts future performance.
items.rationalization: College entrance exam scores predicting first-year college GPA is predictive validity; correlating a new depression test with the Beck Depression Inventory is concurrent.

mnemonic.title: Criterion Validity
mnemonic.phrase: Concurrent is Current, Predictive is Promising Future

items.tosCompetency: Analyze types of validity in educational measurement

items.definition: The degree to which an assessment instrument yields consistent, dependable, and stable scores upon repeated administrations across time or equivalent test forms.
items.rationalization: A test can be reliable without being valid, but a test CANNOT be valid without being reliable. Reliability is a necessary prerequisite for validity.

mnemonic.title: Reliability vs Validity
mnemonic.phrase: Reliability is Consistency, Validity is Truth

items.tosCompetency: Explain reliability concepts and relationship to validity

items.definition: Test-Retest (stability over time), Equivalent Forms (equivalence across parallel sets), Split-Half with Spearman-Brown (internal consistency), Cronbach's Alpha (internal consistency of non-dichotomous items), and Inter-Rater (scorer consistency).
items.rationalization: Split-half halves the test into odd and even items, using Spearman-Brown prophecy formula to calculate full test reliability without retesting.

mnemonic.title: Reliability Methods
mnemonic.phrase: Retest, Parallel, Split-Half, Alpha, Scorer

items.tosCompetency: Compute and interpret reliability coefficients

items.definition: The proportion of total test-takers who answered a test item correctly: p = R / N (where R = number of correct answers, N = total test takers).
items.rationalization: Ranges from 0.00 to 1.00; p < 0.20 is very difficult, 0.21 - 0.80 is desirable/moderate difficulty, and p > 0.80 is very easy.

mnemonic.title: Difficulty Index
mnemonic.phrase: High P Means Plentiful Passed (Easy)
items: High p = Easy, Low p = Difficult

items.tosCompetency: Calculate and interpret item difficulty and discrimination

items.definition: The ability of a test item to differentiate between high-achieving and low-achieving students: D = (RU - RL) / n (where RU = upper group correct, RL = lower group correct, n = group size).
items.rationalization: Ranges from -1.00 to +1.00; D >= 0.40 is very good; 0.30 - 0.39 reasonably good; 0.20 - 0.29 needs revision; D < 0.20 or negative indicates poor item to be discarded.

mnemonic.title: Discrimination Index
mnemonic.phrase: Positive D = Upper Beats Lower Group

items.tosCompetency: Calculate and interpret item difficulty and discrimination

items.definition: A fatal item condition where more students from the lower-scoring group answered the item correctly than students from the upper-scoring group (RL > RU).
items.rationalization: Indicates a miskeyed answer, ambiguous wording, trick phrasing, or that high-achievers overthought the question. The item MUST BE DISCARDED or revised.

mnemonic.title: Negative Discrimination
mnemonic.phrase: Negative Means Discard Immediately

items.tosCompetency: Calculate and interpret item difficulty and discrimination

items.definition: Evaluating the effectiveness of incorrect alternatives in multiple-choice items: a good distractor must attract more students from the lower group than from the upper group and attract at least some students.
items.rationalization: If a distractor attracts zero students, it is non-functioning and must be replaced; if it attracts more upper students, it may be confusing or partially correct.

mnemonic.title: Distractor Efficiency
mnemonic.phrase: Distractors Divert the Lower Scorers

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate distractor efficiency in item analysis

items.definition: A two-way blueprint chart mapping the distribution of test items across instructional content topics and cognitive taxonomy levels (Bloom's).
items.rationalization: Guarantees content validity, prevents teacher test-making bias, and aligns item points with instructional time spent on each competency.

mnemonic.title: Table of Specifications
mnemonic.phrase: TOS: True Outline for Testing Standards

items.tosCompetency: Construct a Table of Specifications (TOS)

items.definition: The 2001 revision of Bloom's cognitive domain using verbs: Remembering (recall), Understanding (explain), Applying (use), Analyzing (break down), Evaluating (judge/justify), and Creating (produce/design).
items.rationalization: Replaced synthesis with creating at the pinnacle and transformed static nouns into active cognitive process verbs.

mnemonic.title: Revised Bloom's
mnemonic.phrase: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create

items.tosCompetency: Classify test items according to Anderson-Krathwohl taxonomy

items.definition: The 5-stage hierarchy of values and attitudes: Receiving (willingness to hear), Responding (active participation), Valuing (attaching worth), Organization (harmonizing values), and Characterization (value internalized into lifestyle).
items.rationalization: Measures emotional growth, social attitudes, and ethical commitment in education.

mnemonic.title: Affective Hierarchy
mnemonic.phrase: Receive, Respond, Value, Organize, Characterize

items.tosCompetency: Formulate affective domain assessment criteria

items.definition: The 7 levels of motor skill acquisition: Perception (sensory cues), Set (readiness), Guided Response (imitation/trial), Mechanism (habitual basic skill), Complex Overt Response (skilled fluid execution), Adaptation (modifying for context), and Origination (creating new movements).
items.rationalization: Essential framework for assessing physical education, technical-vocational skills, laboratory techniques, and artistic performance.

mnemonic.title: Simpson's Psychomotor
mnemonic.phrase: Perceive, Set, Guide, Mechanism, Complex, Adapt, Originate

items.tosCompetency: Formulate psychomotor domain assessment criteria

items.definition: A scoring guide that evaluates student work across multiple distinct, independent criteria or dimensions, assigning separate scores to each criterion.
items.rationalization: Provides granular, diagnostic descriptive feedback, showing learners exactly where they excelled and where they need improvement; takes longer to score than holistic rubrics.

mnemonic.title: Analytic Rubric
mnemonic.phrase: Analyzing Each Attribute Separately

items.tosCompetency: Construct and apply analytic and holistic rubrics

items.definition: A scoring guide that assesses the overall, integrated impression of a student product or performance as a whole, providing a single aggregate score.
items.rationalization: Fast and efficient for large-scale grading and exit evaluations, but provides limited specific feedback on individual weaknesses.

mnemonic.title: Holistic Rubric
mnemonic.phrase: Holistic Gives One Whole Grade

items.tosCompetency: Construct and apply analytic and holistic rubrics

items.definition: A purposeful, systematic collection of student work over time that exhibits the student's efforts, progress, achievements, and self-reflections in one or more areas.
items.rationalization: Includes showcase portfolios (best work), developmental/growth portfolios (working drafts over time), and assessment portfolios (competency evidence).

mnemonic.title: Portfolio Assessment
mnemonic.phrase: Progress, Performance, and Personal Reflection

items.tosCompetency: Implement portfolio assessment and evaluation

items.definition: Norm-referenced compares a student's performance against peer group distribution (ranking / percentiles / grading on a curve); Criterion-referenced evaluates performance against fixed, predetermined standards or rubrics regardless of how others perform.
items.rationalization: DepEd K-12 grading is criterion-referenced; students earn grades based on demonstrating mastery of competencies, not class ranking.

mnemonic.title: Norm vs Criterion
mnemonic.phrase: Norm Compares to Peers, Criterion to Criteria

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate norm-referenced and criterion-referenced assessment

items.definition: Mean is the arithmetic average (sensitive to extreme outliers); Median is the middle score in an ordered distribution (best for skewed data); Mode is the most frequently occurring score (nominal data).
items.rationalization: When test distributions contain extreme high or low scores, the median is the most representative measure of central tendency.

mnemonic.title: Measures of Central Tendency
mnemonic.phrase: Mean is Average, Median is Middle, Mode is Most

items.tosCompetency: Calculate and interpret measures of central tendency

items.definition: The most stable measure of variability indicating how spread out scores are around the distribution mean; the square root of the variance.
items.rationalization: A small SD indicates a homogeneous group clustered close to the mean; a large SD indicates a heterogeneous group with widely scattered scores.

mnemonic.title: Standard Deviation
mnemonic.phrase: Spread of Distribution from the Mean

items.tosCompetency: Compute and interpret measures of variability

items.definition: An asymmetric score distribution with a long tail extending toward high scores on the right, where the majority of students received low scores (Mean > Median > Mode).
items.rationalization: Indicates that the test was very difficult for the class, or students had inadequate preparation.

mnemonic.title: Positively Skewed
mnemonic.phrase: Positive Tail Points Right; Test was Tough

items.tosCompetency: Interpret skewed and normal score distributions

items.definition: An asymmetric score distribution with a long tail extending toward low scores on the left, where the majority of students received high scores (Mode > Median > Mean).
items.rationalization: Indicates that the test was very easy for the class, or students achieved outstanding mastery.

mnemonic.title: Negatively Skewed
mnemonic.phrase: Negative Tail Points Left; Learners Liked It (Easy)

items.tosCompetency: Interpret skewed and normal score distributions

items.definition: A symmetrical bell-shaped score distribution where Mean = Median = Mode, with 68.26% of scores falling within ±1 SD, 95.44% within ±2 SD, and 99.72% within ±3 SD.
items.rationalization: The foundational theoretical model for standard scores and norm-referenced standardized examinations.

mnemonic.title: Normal Curve Rule
mnemonic.phrase: 68-95-99.7 Rule of Bell Curve

items.tosCompetency: Interpret skewed and normal score distributions

items.definition: A standardized score expressing raw score distance from the mean in standard deviation units: z = (X - Mean) / SD.
items.rationalization: Has a mean of 0 and SD of 1; a z-score of +2.0 means the student scored 2 standard deviations above the class average.

mnemonic.title: z-Score Formula
mnemonic.phrase: z = (Score - Mean) divided by SD

items.tosCompetency: Compute and convert standard scores (z, T, Stanine)

items.definition: A transformed standard score that eliminates negative numbers and decimals using the formula: T = 50 + 10(z).
items.rationalization: Has a mean of 50 and SD of 10; a student with z = +1.5 has a T-score of 50 + 10(1.5) = 65.

mnemonic.title: T-Score Formula
mnemonic.phrase: T = Fifty plus Ten times z

items.tosCompetency: Compute and convert standard scores (z, T, Stanine)

items.definition: The percentage of scores in a distribution that fall at or below a specific student's score (e.g., scoring at the 85th percentile means outperforming 85% of test-takers).
items.rationalization: Not a percentage correct score! A student can score 90% correct but be at the 50th percentile if half the group scored higher.

mnemonic.title: Percentile Rank
mnemonic.phrase: Percentile is Percentage Beaten Below

items.tosCompetency: Compute and convert standard scores (z, T, Stanine)

items.term: DepEd Order No. 8, s. 2015 (K to 12 Grading System)
items.definition: The standard grading policy for Basic Education in the Philippines, weighting student grades across three components: Written Work (WW), Performance Tasks (PT), and Quarterly Assessment (QA).
items.rationalization: Abolished knowledge/process/understanding weightings; shifted primary emphasis to Performance Tasks (especially in MAPEH/TLE where PT is 60%).

mnemonic.title: DepEd DO 8 s. 2015
mnemonic.phrase: Written Work, Performance Tasks, Quarterly Assessment

items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd grading policies (DO 8, s. 2015)

items.term: DepEd Component Weights: Languages, AP, ESP
items.definition: Under DO 8, s. 2015: Written Work = 30%, Performance Tasks = 50%, and Quarterly Assessment = 20%.
items.rationalization: Performance tasks have the highest weight, reflecting communicative competence and authentic application in social and value contexts.

mnemonic.title: Languages/AP/ESP Weights
mnemonic.phrase: 30 - 50 - 20 (Written, Performance, Quarterly)

items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd grading policies (DO 8, s. 2015)

items.term: DepEd Component Weights: Science and Mathematics
items.definition: Under DO 8, s. 2015: Written Work = 40%, Performance Tasks = 40%, and Quarterly Assessment = 20%.
items.rationalization: Balanced equal weighting (40-40) between problem-solving/written analysis and laboratory/hands-on performance tasks.

mnemonic.title: Math & Science Weights
mnemonic.phrase: 40 - 40 - 20 (Written, Performance, Quarterly)

items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd grading policies (DO 8, s. 2015)

items.term: DepEd Component Weights: MAPEH and EPP/TLE
items.definition: Under DO 8, s. 2015: Written Work = 20%, Performance Tasks = 60%, and Quarterly Assessment = 20%.
items.rationalization: Heavy 60% emphasis on authentic psychomotor performance tasks, practical demonstrations, and tangible projects.

mnemonic.title: MAPEH & TLE Weights
mnemonic.phrase: 20 - 60 - 20 (Written, Performance, Quarterly)

items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd grading policies (DO 8, s. 2015)

items.term: DepEd Transmutation Table and Passing Mark
items.definition: The initial percentage score is transmuted to a report card grade; the minimum passing grade is 75%, which corresponds to an initial score of 60%.
items.rationalization: Protects learners from mathematical zero penalties and sets a standard baseline of 60% raw performance for mastery certification.

mnemonic.title: DepEd Passing Mark
mnemonic.phrase: 60% Raw Initial Score Transmutes to 75% Passing

items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd grading policies (DO 8, s. 2015)

items.definition: 90-100: Outstanding (O); 85-89: Very Satisfactory (VS); 80-84: Satisfactory (S); 75-79: Fairly Satisfactory (FS); Below 75: Did Not Meet Expectations (DNME).
items.rationalization: Used in formal reporting of quarterly student achievement to parents and school authorities.

mnemonic.title: DepEd Descriptors
mnemonic.phrase: O, VS, S, FS, DNME

items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd grading policies (DO 8, s. 2015)

items.definition: A student who fails (below 75) in up to two learning areas must take remedial classes and pass them; failing three or more learning areas results in retention in the same grade level.
items.rationalization: Provides remedial intervention to prevent immediate retention while ensuring competency mastery before advancement.

mnemonic.title: Remediation Rules
mnemonic.phrase: 1 to 2 Failed = Remedial; 3+ Failed = Retained

items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd grading policies (DO 8, s. 2015)

items.definition: The rater scoring bias where the teacher's overall general positive impression of a student favorably inflates the rating of that student's specific academic performance.
items.rationalization: Avoided by using anonymous scoring (concealing student names) and grading question by question rather than student by student.

mnemonic.title: Halo Effect
mnemonic.phrase: Halo of General Likeability Inflates Scores
items: A - Attractive or liked student favored

items.tosCompetency: Identify and prevent scoring biases (Halo, Horns, Central Tendency)

items.definition: The rater scoring bias where a teacher's negative perception of a student's demeanor or past misconduct unfairly depresses the evaluation of their current academic work.
items.rationalization: Ensuring rubric-guided anonymous evaluation prevents personal biases from harming student ratings.

mnemonic.title: Horns Effect
mnemonic.phrase: Horns of Negative Prejudice Depress Scores
items: N - Negative bias drags score down

items.tosCompetency: Identify and prevent scoring biases (Halo, Horns, Central Tendency)

items.definition: The rater scoring bias where the teacher avoids giving very high or very low ratings, clustering all student evaluations safely in the middle.
items.rationalization: Fails to distinguish exceptional student talent from genuine deficiencies; minimized by clear behavioral rubric anchors.

mnemonic.title: Central Tendency Bias
mnemonic.phrase: Clustering Every Candidate in the Center

items.tosCompetency: Identify and prevent scoring biases (Halo, Horns, Central Tendency)

items.definition: A statistical estimate of the amount of random error associated with a student's test score; SEM = SD * sqrt(1 - Reliability).
items.rationalization: Allows educators to construct a confidence interval (Score ± SEM) around the observed score to reflect the learner's true score.

mnemonic.title: Standard Error of Measurement
mnemonic.phrase: High Reliability Reduces Error of Measurement

items.tosCompetency: Interpret Standard Error of Measurement (SEM)

items.definition: The peakedness or flatness of a distribution curve: Leptokurtic is sharply peaked with clustered scores; Mesokurtic is normally curved; Platykurtic is flat with widely dispersed scores.
items.rationalization: Leptokurtic curves indicate homogeneous student performance; platykurtic indicates high variance and diversity in scores.

mnemonic.title: Kurtosis Types
mnemonic.phrase: Leptokurtic Leaps High, Platykurtic is Plateau Flat

items.tosCompetency: Interpret kurtosis and distribution shapes

items.definition: A 9-point normalized standard rating scale with a mean of 5 and standard deviation of 2, dividing the normal bell curve into 9 bands (1 lowest, 9 highest).
items.rationalization: Scores 4, 5, and 6 represent average performance (spanning 54% of the population).

mnemonic.title: Stanine Scale
mnemonic.phrase: Standard Nine: 1 to 9 with 5 as Center

items.tosCompetency: Compute and convert standard scores (z, T, Stanine)

items.definition: The principle that Intended Learning Outcomes (ILOs), Teaching and Learning Activities (TLAs), and Assessment Tasks (ATs) must be completely aligned and coherent.
items.rationalization: If the ILO requires students to 'analyze arguments', teaching must involve analytical exercises and the test must assess analysis—not rote memorization.

mnemonic.title: Constructive Alignment
mnemonic.phrase: Outcomes, Activities, and Assessments in Harmony

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate constructive alignment across instructional design

items.definition: The direct impact and influence that tests and high-stakes examinations exert on teaching, curriculum, and student study habits.
items.rationalization: Can be positive (tests encourage rigorous reading and problem solving) or negative (teachers teach to the test, abandoning unassessed creative inquiry).

mnemonic.title: Washback Effect
mnemonic.phrase: What is Tested Washes Back into What is Taught

items.tosCompetency: Analyze the social and educational impact of testing (washback)

items.definition: An assessment mode that compares a learner's current performance against their own prior personal performance rather than against other students or external criteria.
items.rationalization: Highly motivating for struggling learners and special education students; highlights personal effort, persistence, and self-growth.

mnemonic.title: Ipsative Assessment
mnemonic.phrase: Ipsative: Improving Past Self

items.tosCompetency: Differentiate norm-referenced, criterion-referenced, and ipsative assessment

items.definition: Assessment practices where students use clear rubrics to evaluate their own work (self-assessment) or their classmates' work (peer-assessment), providing constructive feedback.
items.rationalization: Promotes metacognition, critical appraisal, objectivity, and autonomous accountability for learning standards.

mnemonic.title: Self & Peer Assessment
mnemonic.phrase: Students Scoring Standards Systematically

items.tosCompetency: Implement self and peer assessment protocols

items.definition: Professional rules for drafting objective items: Stem must present a single clear problem; avoid negative stems (use capitalized NOT/EXCEPT if needed); alternatives must be grammatically parallel; avoid 'All of the above' or 'None of the above'.
items.rationalization: 'All of the above' allows guessing with only two recognized correct options; negative stems increase cognitive reading load instead of measuring content mastery.

mnemonic.title: Multiple Choice Rules
mnemonic.phrase: Clear Stem, Plausible Distractors, Avoid All/None

items.tosCompetency: Apply best practices in crafting multiple-choice test items
